chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Ibn Abi Nabil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is an obligation on the poor to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) once a year, and it is an obligation on the wealthy to visit it twice a year.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of times one should visit the grave of Imam Husayn annually according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a baseline for the spiritual obligation of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s shrine, distinguishing between the poor and the wealthy based on their capacity for travel and devotion. While some scholars interpret the term 'haqq' (right/obligation) here as recommended (mustahabb) rather than strictly mandatory (wajib), the distinction highlights the Islamic principle that religious duties are scaled to one’s means. This practice reinforces the enduring connection between the living community and the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a tangible expression of love and remembrance.
